deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is Dedekind's 1878 setting, 'Über den Zusammenhang zwischen der Theorie der Ideale und der Theorie der höheren Congruenzen'. F(t) is a monic irreducible integer polynomial of degree n and θ is a root of F. Let O be the ring of algebraic integers of Q(θ). A prime p is 'of the second kind' if it divides the index [O : Z[θ]]. By the criterion of §1, this happens exactly when some polynomial G(t) of degree < n, with coefficients not all divisible by p, has G(θ)/p ∈ O.

The 'obige Darstellung' (earlier representation) is not on this page. From the way A, B, M are used, it is presumably F = A·B + p·M. Here A, B, M ∈ Z[t] come from the factorisation of F mod p, as in Dedekind's 1878 setup (for example A = product of the distinct irreducible factors, B = cofactor). This identification is my inference.

Purpose. Dedekind remarks that it is more convenient ('zweckmäßig') to settle the statements of §3 already in §2. He then proves the direction: if A, B, M have a common nonconstant factor E mod p, then p is of the second kind.

Step 1. E (written ε / 𝔈) is a common divisor of A, B, M mod p. So there are integer polynomials with
- A = E·A1 + p·A2
- B = E·B1 + p·B2
- M = E·M1 + p·M2

Step 2. Substitute into F = AB + pM [expansion mine]:
F = E²·A1B1 + E·p·(A1B2 + A2B1 + M1) + p²·(A2B2 + M2).
This is the page's form F = 𝔛E² + 𝔜Ep + ℨp², with 𝔛 = A1B1, 𝔜 = A1B2 + A2B1 + M1, ℨ = A2B2 + M2.

Step 3. Put ε = E(θ), ξ = 𝔛(θ), η = 𝔜(θ), ζ = ℨ(θ). These are algebraic integers in Z[θ]. Since F(θ) = 0:
ξε² + ηεp + ζp² = 0.

Step 4. Multiply by ξ/p²:
(ξε/p)² + η·(ξε/p) + ξζ = 0.
So ξε/p is a root of a monic quadratic whose coefficients η and ξζ are algebraic integers.

Step 5. A root of a monic polynomial with algebraic-integer coefficients is an algebraic integer. Dedekind cites Dirichlet–Dedekind Zahlentheorie: §160.3 of the 2nd edition (1871), §160.2 of the 3rd (1879), §173.5 of the 4th (1894); also §13.2° of 'Sur la théorie des nombres entiers algébriques' (1877). Hence ξε/p ∈ O, i.e. ξε is divisible by p.

Step 6 (continued on the facing page, whose text shows through mirrored at the top). Modulo p we have F ≡ 𝔛E², and E is not constant mod p. So the polynomial 𝔛E, which takes the value ξε at t = θ, has degree n − deg E < n mod p and is not ≡ 0 mod p. Therefore p is of the second kind by §1. Q.E.D. The facing page is dated 1895.8.22.
errors: No genuine error. Small gap: '𝔛E has degree < n' holds only modulo p, i.e. after reducing coefficients mod p (or for suitably chosen representatives). Strictly one should replace 𝔛E by a polynomial G of degree < n with G ≡ 𝔛E mod p. Then G(θ)/p = ξε/p + (integral element) is still integral, and G is not ≡ 0 mod p because F is not ≡ 0 mod p. The proof is easily repaired.
One also needs deg(E mod p) ≥ 1 and the leading coefficient of 𝔛E not divisible by p. These are implicit in 'ε keine Constante' and F monic.

results.what: If the factors A, B and the 'error term' M in F = AB + pM share a nonconstant common factor mod p, then p divides the index [O_K : Z[θ]]. Proved by writing F = 𝔛E² + 𝔜Ep + ℨp² and showing (𝔛E)(θ)/p is integral via a monic quadratic.
results.modern_name: Dedekind's criterion (one direction) for p dividing the index of Z[θ] / p-maximality of Z[θ]; related to the Dedekind–Kummer theorem

results.what: Integrality of a root of a monic polynomial with algebraic-integer coefficients (transitivity of integrality), cited from Dirichlet–Dedekind and the 1877 memoir

deep.surprise_reason: This is a 1895 reworking: a short alternative proof, reorganising §§2–3, of one direction of Dedekind's own 1878 index criterion. It is a nice unpublished detail but entirely consistent with known Dedekind work.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, expand; E,p,A1,A2,B1,B2,M1,M2=symbols('E p A1 A2 B1 B2 M1 M2'); A=E*A1+p*A2; B=E*B1+p*B2; M=E*M1+p*M2; X=A1*B1; Y=A1*B2+A2*B1+M1; Z=A2*B2+M2; expand(A*B+p*M-(X*E**2+Y*E*p+Z*p**2))==0
checkable.asserts: F = AB + pM takes the form 𝔛E² + 𝔜Ep + ℨp² when E divides A, B, M modulo p

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, expand; x,e,y,z,p=symbols('xi epsilon eta zeta p'); expand((x/p**2)*(x*e**2+y*e*p+z*p**2) - ((x*e/p)**2 + y*(x*e/p) + x*z))==0
checkable.asserts: Multiplying ξε²+ηεp+ζp²=0 by ξ/p² gives (ξε/p)² + η(ξε/p) + ξζ = 0

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, Poly; t=symbols('t'); F=t**2+3; p=2; # F ≡ (t+1)^2 mod 2, A=B=t+1, M=(F-(t+1)**2)/2 = -t+1 ≡ t+1 mod 2; ((1+t)/2).subs(t, (-3)**0.5) # (1+sqrt(-3))/2 is integral
checkable.asserts: Example: for F=t²+3, p=2, A, B, M share the factor t+1 mod 2, and indeed (1+θ)/2 is integral, so 2 divides the index of Z[√-3]

transcription_corrections: The first line most likely reads 'zweckmäßig ist' or 'zweckmäßiger ist', not 'zuverlässig[?] ist'.

The mirrored bleed-through in the upper lines is the text of the facing page ('...entiers algébriques) die ganze Zahl ξε theilbar durch p ... (1895. 8. 22)'). That text is the continuation of this argument, so the logical order is this page then the facing page.
The polynomial whose value at θ is ε is a Fraktur 𝔈 (E); in the displayed F = 𝔛ε² + 𝔜εp + ℨp², ε stands for that polynomial 𝔈.
'die Sätze von §. 3 schon in §. 2 zu erledigen' — the preposition is probably 'in', not 'von'.
